chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The shortening [of prayer] is in a Bareyd, and the Bareyd is four Farsakhs.

key_terms.بَرِيدٍ: A unit of distance known as a Bareyd
key_terms.فَرَاسِخَ: Farsakhs, a traditional unit of distance

ai.seo_question: What is the distance in Farsakhs at which a Muslim traveler must shorten their prayer?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the foundational metric for the distance of travel (Masafat al-Tariq) required to shorten the four-rak'ah prayers, defining a 'Bareyd' as four 'Farsakhs'. In Shia jurisprudence, this narration is critical for determining the minimum threshold for Qasr, with scholars historically debating whether this distance is measured one-way or round-trip. It underscores the practical ease (Taysir) granted to travelers, linking physical distance directly to the modification of ritual worship.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The shortening is in a Bareyd, and the Bareyd is of four Farsakhs (approximately 12 miles)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Salah (prayer) is reduced after traveling a distance of one barid and one barid is four farasikh (which is twelve miles).”’
